rationale: Excluded as wrong topic (E01). The article offers methodological reflections on the economic and ecological impacts of the Arco Norte regional road, bridge, deep-water port, hydro-electricity and telecommunications infrastructure corridor across Northern Amazonia and the Guiana Shield, with no connection to household or community water or sanitation service access.
plain_vs_narrow_note: No difference between plain and narrow Criterion 2 readings: the record is clearly out of scope under Criterion 1 and Criterion 4 because it examines transport, port, hydropower and telecommunications infrastructure impacts rather than household or community water or sanitation service access.

evidence_quotes.quote: Arco Norte is a road project designed and created by Brazil, linking the northern part of Brazil with the three Guianas: Guyana, Suriname and French Guyana, and with the Caribbean Sea.

The road project is part of a larger programme to integrate the state of Roraima with Guyana through the construction of a deep-water port, a hydro-electricity facility in Guyana and the development of high-speed dependable communications systems in the region.
